sonnet.problem: Verse 28 repeats the fact from verse 7: Laish was far from Sidon and had no alliance with anyone. Stop 1 card 11 already asked about it, so this card asks the same fact a second time. Whether Sidon sends help is just the 'no alliance' point again.
sonnet.rule: When a line repeats in the passage, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears in this passage.

sonnet.problem: The joke implies the priest said so little because he was afraid of the six hundred armed men. Verse 17 says only that he stood at the gate with them. The text gives no reason for his brief words, and the card adds one as if it were the reason.
sonnet.rule: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

sonnet.problem: The right answer stands out. It is the only one that is not an 'Until...' phrase, and it is the longest. It also copies the Bible's own wording ('the whole time the house of God was in Shiloh'), while both wrong answers are plain modern phrasing.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
